content.content:
61	
62	*Co-op beats* — a crewmate already at the object as the visible reason for `BUSY`, the revive channel on a downed crewmate, the friendly-harm act — are Vertical Slice B. The MVP fantasy rests on your own hands.
63	
64	**Pillar quotes the section carries.** Pillar 4, verbatim: "No lie is unfalsifiable: the truth is always available through the physical world, a second instrument, a saner crewmate, the human channel, or time — and checking costs time, risk or trust." The deferred outcome (IA-12) is that sentence made into a mechanic: the check is *time* (the full bar), *risk* (standing still, lit, noisy) and never free. Pillar 3: "The players' light, noise, power use and restraint raise or lower its attention… Restraint and stealth are real strategies" — every channel is lit, stationary and noisy; restraint means choosing which jobs to do. Pillar 1: "A pipe may *look* fixed, but the room still gets cold, the air still thins, the pressure still drops" — every verb's result is a consequence-channel change; Interaction writes none of it itself (Failure & Trail, row 15: "no data crosses"). Pillar 2: "Every breach is preceded by a tell a careful player could have perceived" — the player's own verbs are exogenous (LS-13) and carry their own tell (a severed stub's hiss, the inrush flicker), and a verb never outruns a tell because movement always cancels. Pillar 5: "losing the home-ship or a crewmate costs ship and body, never knowledge" — a patch is free but decays, a FULL repair costs a part that comes from deeper, and nothing a verb teaches is lost on death (restart from the last autosave, Save/Load SL-7).
65	
66	**Design tests.** *Primary:* when a choice makes an action cheaper to do than to be sure of, make the checking cheaper than the lie, never free; when a prompt could be drawn where `lit(ref)` is false, never draw it — a prompt must not lie by omission. *Subordinate:* (1) **"I can leave now" (P2)** — when a verb could hold the player in place versus let any move release them, release them; fails if any verb, at any sanity, rhythm or Attention level, holds the body. (2) **The prompt never answers (P4)** — when a prompt, cue or rejection could reveal module-body truth at zero time, risk or trust versus only after the full channel, after the channel; fails if a player can learn a pipe's real state by tapping and releasing, or by pressing a FULL repair, cancelling at any tick and reading the part stock, the weight cue or the reserved bucket. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: and by a one-block PATCH tap-and-cancel, whose Graph state, descriptors and noise are identical at hp 10000, 5999, 5000 and 4000 with `hp_cap` 10000, because the PATCH guard of IA-17 makes no M7 call there; AC-IA-26.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: from the first credited block on, a cancel, abort or restore consumes the part in both truth branches, so believing a lie and acting on it costs a part, which is honest under P4; only a channel that runs to its end may return the part, IA-18.)* (3) **No stat penalties from interactions (P4 secondary)** — a −10 % repair speed at low sanity versus a false gauge: the false gauge; channel durations are fixed per verb and read no sanity, Attention, rhythm or device. (4) **The hands work only in the light (P3)** — act without light versus require light: require light; exactly three listed object exceptions (actor verbs, `throw_glowstick` and the self-patch, have no object to light, IA-6) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. (5) **Physical answer, not message (P1)** — a "repaired!" toast versus the hiss stopping: the hiss; completion is a cue, the result is the world.
67	
68	**How the fantasy deepens under hallucination — and must not break.** The rule of the section: *the prompt never answers; the work does.* Prompt existence is a function of the object's declared kind, the tool in hand, `lit` and `in_reach` only (IA-11), so the prompt says the same thing to a sane and to a hallucinating player. What hallucination changes is what the player *believes before* reaching, and the work is how they find out.
69	- **A hallucinated-broken, truly healthy pipe (false system state):** the sprite and gauge read broken. The prompt appears (it is kind-based); the bar runs the full 180 ticks, pixel- and sound-identical to a real patch; the Graph receives zero mutator calls; the job resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` and the *nothing happened* cue. "Three seconds of noise for nothing — it wasn't broken. My eyes are going." The check cost time, noise and light; it was never free.
70	- **A hallucinated-fixed, truly leaking pipe (hp 2000):** looks whole, gauge green. The prompt still appears; if the player patches anyway, the real increments land against 2000. The cold is the truth (P1): the cautious player who patches a "fixed" pipe is rewarded by physics, not by a message.
71	- **A phantom entity:** no subject, so never lit, never focused, never prompted; `interact` with no focus is a silent no-op with no cue and no pre-play. **A claim correction the section must carry:** reaching for a thing falsifies *objects*, not monsters — real HORROR subjects also take no verb at MVP, so a missing prompt is not evidence about a monster either way (true at MVP; in Vertical Slice B IA-31's precondition keeps the plate from discriminating real horrors from crewmates drawn as horrors). That symmetry is by design; the truth about monsters lives in the footprint of the world (sound, frost, hull stress), not in the hands.
72	- **Phantom salvage (a real registered `junk_` item):** every verb works normally, because it is a real item. The truth is the weight cue (Suit), the scanner field check (`FIELD_CHECK_TICKS`, scanner in hand) or the trip home — the cheaper check that Pillar 4(d) requires.
73	- **A crewmate rendered as a horror (Vertical Slice B):** for an actor whose Sanity level is below the harm threshold the prompt reads the equipped tool's ordinary verb (`E · Cut`), never a target noun; a sane actor gets no prompt and a forced attempt is rejected `NOT_ELIGIBLE`. The horror is that the hands work. (Two rulings travel with this bullet. IA-31's **blocking Vertical Slice B precondition**: the plate must not tell a crewmate drawn as a horror from a real horror, so real horrors carry a `repel` declaration with the same `verb_name_key` and the eligibility bit is the class-(c) render level. And the **self-knowledge ruling**: the plate's presence is honest knowledge of the actor's *own* sanity, which Pillar 4 allows.)
74	
75	**Reference techniques — adopt / reject.**
76	
77	| Reference | Technique | Verdict | Why |
78	|---|---|---|---|
79	| Project Zomboid | Timed contextual actions on a linear bar, cancelled by moving; no skill-check minigame | **Adopt** | Exactly the channel model (IA-14); the designer's touchstone |
80	| Project Zomboid | Skill levels that shorten action time or cut failure chance | **Reject** | Progression from repair (the Graph writes none, LS-23); would break bar-length identity between a real and a hallucinated job |
81	| Pandorum | Chest-mounted, hands-free lamp: both hands work while lit | **Adopt** | User decision; the beam stays on the job and while carrying |
82	| Barotrauma | Stationary hold-to-repair where interruption is the player's choice, under pressure | **Adopt (the stationary hold)** | The breach-rhythm pressure of Pillar 2 |
83	| Barotrauma | Repair minigame (sliders, wiring) | **Reject** | A minigame is a QTE in disguise (no QTE anywhere) and a UI surface that could leak module-body truth |
84	| Generic action games | Round or dial-shaped progress and confirm indicators; verb menus | **Reject** | Art bible 3.4 / 7.3 and HR-14: the bar is linear with a needle-mark; one contextual action |
85	| Dead Space | Diegetic UI on the character and in the world | **Reject for prompts; adopt the spirit for results** | The prompt is explicitly meta (art bible 7.0) so it can never be corrupted into a lie; results are diegetic (hiss, cold) |
86	| Prompts that name the outcome ("Repair broken pipe") | Verb plus object state | **Reject** | A free oracle under Pillar 4(b); the prompt never names condition |
87	
88	**Tone and language.** Use: reach, hands, hold, the bar, step away, let go, patch, cut, cap, crank, close the breaker, open the valve, throw a glowstick, check, in the light, the edge, chest lamp, beam, go dark, the hiss thins, the room warms, nothing happened. Avoid in player-facing text and in fantasy prose: attack, strike, hit, damage, kill, "target" as an on-screen noun, "failed" or "can't" as a rejection string (the kernel never displays strings), "success!", "repaired!", minigame, QTE, combo, skill, level up, XP, "health" for modules (say the pipe holds or leaks), flashlight or torch for the beam, visibility, stealth, detection, hidden. Prompt grammar is locked by the art bible: keybind plus verb, `E · Patch`, never condition, never target.
89	
90	**Anti-pillar guard rails (stated as fiction as well as rule).**
91	1. *Not a combat game.* There is no attack input. The friendly-harm act is an ordinary tool verb on a crewmate, gated on the *actor's* authoritative Sanity level, lethal against a victim who cannot or does not respond, with the moment of death being Suit's rule (IA-31; "death is a bitch. It happens." — user), with no reward, no counter, no XP and no attribution inside Interaction: one `record_harm_event` call is made to Sanity (registry: `record_harm_event`), which attributes it to the web. Horrors take no verb at MVP; tools repel through Horror and Attention, and nothing is attacked.
92	2. *No intentional PvP.* A sane actor sees no prompt on a crewmate and is rejected `NOT_ELIGIBLE` if they force the attempt.
93	3. *Not a freeform builder.* Weld, section cut and install are pre-shaped and Assembly's; Interaction only declares which button starts them.
94	4. *No meter, no readout, no tooltip.* No interaction stat, no weight readout, no numeric or bar sanity readout, no "you can't do that because…" string; a rejection is a cue, never a shake. **One ruled exception (CD-GDD-ALIGN, recorded):** the actor's *own* sanity level is honest self-knowledge, which Pillar 4 allows. The concept makes the harm gate "verifiably below threshold" and gives the attacker "a visible sanity sign" (CON:252), so the presence of the friendly-harm prompt, and the immediate `NOT_ELIGIBLE` on a forced attempt, are a permitted one-bit statement about the actor's own state and about nothing in the world: no module, no figure, no hallucination class. The prompt is not a gauge of anything else (IA-31).
95	5. *No reward path for work.* No repair score, salvage bonus or faster hands; the reward of a patch is a warm room.
96	
97	**Trade-off accepted.** Some jobs will be three seconds of noise for nothing: the deferred outcome is the price of a sanity system that is not a free lie-detector. We accept that a minority of players will call it "the game wasted my time" in exchange for the majority learning "my eyes are lying." The mitigation is diegetic — the consequence channel (cold, hiss, draught, heat shimmer) lets a careful player decide *before* reaching; reading the world is always cheaper than reaching for it. **We will know this was right if** playtesters describe a failed job as "it wasn't really broken" or "it was still too hot" rather than "the game wouldn't let me" or "bug"; no playtester asks for a "why can't I" message and, asked how they knew a pipe was really fixed, they answer with a physical sign (the cold stopped, the hiss stopped) rather than a UI element; players step away mid-channel when they hear something and do not report feeling punished; and a review finds no channel duration, reason class or prompt rule whose inputs include sanity, Attention, rhythm or device. **Pass/fail threshold:** the attribution half of these criteria is a playtest row, AC-IA-73b (at least 7 of 8 testers who receive a deferred outcome explain it with a physical cause rather than "bug" or "the game wouldn't let me"); a miss re-opens this trade-off, first by strengthening the consequence channel's legibility and never by adding a reason string. The cost to Challenge is therefore measured, not assumed. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review, two additions. (1) The hands answer the world; the scanner answers Sanity. A `field_check` is the cheap way to debunk a lie about an object and is deliberately priced (a tool in hand, `FIELD_CHECK_TICKS`, TOOL noise); a hand job answers what is true of the pipe, at the price of its whole bar. The scanner therefore dominates hand-checking as a way to resolve a hallucination, and that is accepted: it resolves the lie, not the leak (Open Question 32 keeps the repair completion from debunking). (2) The Pillar 3 price of working has to be perceivable: a TOOL push with no tell is a hidden stat. The tell is Attention's (its noise-driven tell and consequence, the owner named in IA-33) voiced by Adaptive Audio; Interaction supplies only the class. AC-IA-136 is the playtest row: a consequence within about 10 s of a TOOL push, named by most testers.)*
98	
99	**What this section does not claim.** The cost of light (Emitter State) and of noise (Attention); the body's honesty and the focus model (Controller); the physics of the hiss, the cold and `BLOCKED` reasons (Graph); trails (Failure & Trail); vitals, charges, the weight cue and death (Suit); what a scanner reveals, the harm threshold, scars and the victim's tell (Sanity, Perception Filter); prompt and bar pixels (HUD); cue sound design (Adaptive Audio). Interaction owns which verb a press means, when it is accepted, how long it takes, and when the answer arrives.
100	
101	## Detailed Design
102	
103	### Core Rules
104	
105	*Conventions.* Rules are numbered `IA-n` (Interaction Act); formulas `D.n` (Formulas section); invariants `I-n`; acceptance criteria `AC-IA-n`; diagnostics `IA_*`. Durations are in ticks (`TICK_RATE` 60); the one seconds-denominated knob, `FULL_JOB_GRACE_S`, converts with the kernel's `ticks_for_seconds`. "Class A" and "Class B" are the Graph's mutator classes (LS-18: Class A is command-backed and paired with a pure `check_*`; Class B is unconditional, clamps and never rejects). Every contract with a system that has no GDD on disk is tagged `(provisional — X undesigned)`; the names given for those contracts are proposals the neighbour must adopt or replace. A contract with a designed sibling is tagged `(Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-n)` or `(Layout, Designed — LY-n)` and uses the names that GDD publishes (the owner of an interface is the system that publishes it). Where an owner GDD spells only some names of a pattern, an inferred name is tagged as inferred at its first use. Upstream constants and formulas (`in_reach`, `lit(ref)` hysteresis, `fairness_gate`, `repair_part_for`, `salvage_yield`, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` and the rest of the cited list under Tuning Knobs) are used by registry name where registered, else by the owner GDD's own identifier (Cross-References section 5 lists the 12 names not yet registered), and never restated; where this GDD needs a different value that is a CONFLICT, surfaced in Open Questions, never a silent change. Each rule names what decides it ("*Decides:*") and, where one existed, the alternative considered. Where the four specialist proposals disagreed and the advisor rulings were silent, the choice is marked "(orchestrator ruling: …)". Where a specialist proposed a departure from an advisor ruling and the checkpoint rejected it (DEP-1, DEP-3), the ruling stays in the text and the departure is recorded in Open Questions as a closed alternative with the checkpoint reason.

107	**Group A — Ownership, declaration, focus and the lit-only rule**
108	
109	**IA-1 Interaction is the verb layer, not a doer of everything.** Interaction (a) declares, per focused object and equipped tool, which command type and mode a press of `interact` means; (b) registers the command types whose effect is its own (IA-3); (c) owns channel progress, partial-progress persistence, pickup, drop, throw, the field check, the friendly-harm act and revive; (d) is the caller of the Graph's Class A mutators M6 to M9 and M11 to M13 (M10 has no MVP verb) for the player verbs, of the Class B M16 for V7 top-up, and of Emitter State's subject registration (E6, E7, E8) and `spawn_deployable` (E3); (e) publishes exactly three Class B mutators (`sync_section`, `place_loose`, and `open_channel` for owner-registered channels, IA-35), two read views (`focus_view`, `channel_view`) and one pure derived read (`last_salvage_T()`, IA-25), and nothing else. It never draws, never subscribes to results and never calls presentation (kernel CR-10); it uses no RNG and no wall-clock (every outcome is a deterministic function of block state, true Graph state and the tick); it holds no scene-tree reference (H10). *Decides:* advisor R1, guard G1, kernel CR-10.
110	
111	**IA-2 The declaration table is data.** One row per (object class, tool requirement) under `assets/data/interaction/verbs/` — the folder the Controller's lint already scans. Fields: `verb_id` (a V-id or an Interaction id); `object_class` (BREAKER_PANEL, VALVE, DOOR_FACE, VENT_HATCH, REPAIRABLE, SALVAGE_MODULE, CRANK_MACHINE, WELD_SOCKET, STUB, LOOSE_ITEM, SWITCH_FIXTURE, ACTOR, ACTOR_SELF, TOPUP_PORT, INSTRUMENT, HARDPOINT, CONSOLE (two classes, POD_CONSOLE and DOCK_CONSOLE, told apart by Layout's `console_role`, IA-40 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ASK-CT-13 / ASK-CT-14 accepted, delegated G6, GAP)*); one interactable may carry several classes — a scrubber is both REPAIRABLE and SALVAGE_MODULE); `command_type`; `owner_system`; `mode` in {TAP, HOLD_CONFIRM, CHANNEL}; `tool_required` (a def id or NONE); `noise_class` in {QUIET, TOOL, LOUD}; `duration_key` (names a registered constant, never a literal); `reason_classes` (per reason, IMMEDIATE or DEFERRED); `verb_name_key` (a localisation key; always state-neutral, IA-11); `eligible` (an optional predicate name; at MVP: Sanity's `actor_sanity_below_harm_threshold` (registry; IA-31), Assembly's `weld_offer` and `seam_cut_offer` (registry; IA-23) and Web Map's `console_ready(role)`, with `berthed_present()` for the two DOCK_CONSOLE rows (WM-8; IA-40); an owner-supplied predicate is evaluated exactly as Interaction's own and reads no module-body field, IA-11b); `admitted_while_carrying` (bool, default false; true only on the HARDPOINT `install_module` row, the POD_CONSOLE `pod_hop` row and the door `set_opening` row, IA-28; *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the door row added*) (registry: `admitted_while_carrying`); `destructive` (bool); `priority` (int, for IA-5); `subject_allowed` (bool, so that in-wall cable and duct edges are repaired at their visible junction, not along their length). The table takes **no** sanity, Attention, rhythm, breach, device or hold-versus-toggle input (lint, IA-4). A pull request that adds a verb is one data row, one handler and one registration line, with an empty Adapter diff (Controller acceptance stub at PCI:969; kernel velocity rule, KRN:135). *Decides:* R1, R26, PC-6.
112	
113	**IA-3 One command type per verb; `interact` is an input action.** Each verb is its own command type with its own `validate`, reason subset, `max_age_ticks` 120 (`MAX_AGE_TICKS_ACTION`; `STALE` is unreachable from local ingress), `coalesce NONE` (edge-triggered), `actor_binding OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `allowed_origins {PLAYER}` and not `allowed_when_paused`. Payloads are primitives only (kernel CR-4): a registered subject ref (or a PlayerId for `begin_harm` and `begin_revive`) and, for `throw_glowstick`, `aim_angle` — **never a believed state, a direction, a verb choice or a kind** (LS-22; the one enum, `field_check`'s closed `check_kind` {SCAN}, names the instrument's check, not a subject's kind). 138	
139	Interaction **declares** the rows it does not register (their `verb_name_key`, mode, tool and noise class live in the declaration table) and **registers** the rest; `set_opening` alone admits `SYSTEM` origin, for a failure cascade's door close (IA-24). *Alternative considered:* one generic `interact {target, verb}` command with an internal dispatcher — rejected: one giant `validate`, mixed reason sets, per-verb age and coalescing impossible, replay logs less legible. *Stale tokens routed:* the kernel text at KRN:85 and KRN:204 lists `interact` as a command; here it is an input action only. KRN:85 (and IDB:470) also list `use_item`, which no GDD registers: Suit registers exactly `equip_tool` and states `use_item` is not its command (SE-40, AC-SE-39), so it is removed from this table and routed to the kernel and Item DB owners as a stale token; the suppressant's effect verb (Suit's `consume_charge`) is declared here when Attention or Horror register it, and no MVP row exists (Cross-References). *Decides:* R1, R2, PC-6, LS-22, Controller acceptance at PCI:969.
140	
141	**IA-4 Focus is the Controller's; Interaction re-validates; no rule branches on device.** The Adapter chooses exactly one focused object by the aim-weighted score (`FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT`, `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN`; ties go to the smaller aim angle, then the smaller entity id; Controller D.9) and submits the *declared* type with that ref. The simulation never computes a score; it re-validates the chosen target with `in_reach` (`REACH_PX`, `REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG`, `COS2_REACH`; cited, not restated) and `lit`. There is no pick-under-cursor path on any device. A gamepad user who never touches the right stick focuses by facing (aim follows movement until the first right-stick input, PC-4/5); `interact` with no focus is an Adapter no-op — no command, no pre-play, no cue. No Interaction rule reads the input device, hold-versus-toggle or tap-to-confirm policy (Adapter policy, PC-7 and PC-13); lint: `assets/data/interaction/verbs` takes no sanity, Attention, rhythm, breach or device input. *Decides:* PC-6, R26, T8.
142	
143	**IA-5 One contextual action: `select_verb`.** Given the focused object's classes and the tool in hand (Suit's `tool_in_hand`, Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-40), the declaration row is chosen by: (1) the rows whose `tool_required` equals the tool in hand, lowest `priority` first; else (2) the bare-hand rows, lowest `priority` first; else (3) the lowest-`priority` row of the class, shown with its tool glyph and answered `NO_TOOL` on press. The choice is a function of (object classes, tool in hand, the `eligible` predicate) only — **never of hp, state, forced mode or served power** (IA-11). While the actor carries a module, the only selectable rows are `drop` placement and the declared carry-admitted rows (`admitted_while_carrying`: `install_module` on a HARDPOINT whose `compatible_defs(h)` lists the carried instance's def, `pod_hop` on the POD_CONSOLE, and V4 `set_opening` on a door face; IA-28) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; any other world target while carrying is shown no prompt at all. *Example:* a scrubber with the welder in hand selects V1 `begin_patch`; with the cutter in hand it selects V8 `begin_cut`; with bare hands row (3) selects V1 and shows the welder glyph — the press answers `NO_TOOL`. *Alternatives considered:* hide the verb without the tool (the player never learns it exists); auto-equip the right tool (removes a Suit decision and makes `equip_tool` pointless). *Decides:* R11, HR-14 (one contextual action), D10.
144	
145	**IA-6 Act only on what is lit (`act_gate`).** `act_gate(o) = in_reach(o) AND lit(o)`, where `in_reach` is the Controller's integer predicate (itself including the lit conjunct) and `lit` is Emitter State's hysteresis bit (`LIT_ON_PM`, `LIT_OFF_PM`, no dwell). Every PLAYER-origin Interaction command whose declaration is not exempt checks `act_gate` in `validate`, against the exposure table committed at tick T−1 (EM-25). The exceptions are exactly three, plus the actor verbs that are not object verbs: `drop` of the carried module, `toggle_beam`, and the inspect card of an already-lit instrument (PC-6); `throw_glowstick` is an actor verb like `toggle_beam` and needs no lit target (IA-29); and **the self-patch is an actor verb too**: `begin_patch` on object class `ACTOR_SELF` (IA-17) targets the actor's own suit, so there is no object to light and no reach to test; its declaration row has `exempt(row) = 1`, `validate` skips both `in_reach` and `lit` for it, and an ACTOR_SELF row can produce neither `OUT_OF_RANGE` nor `NOT_LIT`. This is not a fourth object exception: the object list stays exactly three (`drop`, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card of an already-lit instrument), and the pod-console refusal below is unchanged. The dark self-patch is still priced, so it is not a free Attention dodge (Pillar 3): TOOL noise on every accrued tick (IA-33), 180 stationary ticks (`PATCH_CHANNEL_TICKS`) and the welder in hand. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs)* **No fourth exception for the pod console (refused, stated here):** Web Map's ASK-I2 and Boarding's ASK-BS-I3 ask that `pod_hop` at the CONSOLE be exempt from the lit condition; the three exceptions are the Controller's PC-6 list (PCI:127) and IA-17 already refuses a fourth, so `pod_hop`, `berth` and `unberth` stay lit-gated (on both the POD_CONSOLE and the DOCK_CONSOLE subject, IA-40), and the hop stays available by content, not by exemption: the docked pod's dock-room prop carries a small self-powered status glow that counts as an ordinary lit fixture (not a fourth `act_gate` exception), so `pod_hop`'s lit gate is always satisfied at the console and a `NOT_LIT` at a dock console is a content defect, not a state (Open Question 31, resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2, Web Map option (B); this refusal STANDS. The self-powered fixture class (Emitter State EM-3 / EM-11), the placement rule and lint in every dock room (Derelict Authoring), the art-director's luminance separation from the visible-unknown lamp and Web Map accepting ASK-BS-W3 are the other owners' sides; Boarding's BS-19 invariant is owned jointly: Web Map and Emitter State guarantee the glow, Authoring lints its placement)*. An unregistered ref answers exactly as an unlit one (EM-21), so a phantom and a darkened real object are indistinguishable by design. *Why the rule exists:* it makes darkness a trade, not a free dodge of the web's attention — "unlit objects can be worked on" was rejected because working in the dark would be a free Attention dodge. Pillars: **P3** (every action spends exposure) and **P4** (reaching for a phantom finds nothing). *Decides:* PC-6, EM-21/22/25, F2 (the composite is registered as a formula, D.2).

147	**IA-7 Mid-channel re-check.** Each channel re-reads `lit(target)` through the same query at the cadence of IA-14 (every `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS`, counted from the begin tick, inclusive) and aborts with cause UNLIT if it is false at a check; a dark gap shorter than the cadence is tolerated (at most `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS − 1` = 5 dark channel ticks, Emitter State AC-59b). The geometric conjuncts of `in_reach` are re-tested at the same cadence (OUT_OF_REACH). Neither re-check is tested for a record whose target class is ACTOR_SELF (exempt, IA-6); such a record's abort set is IA-14 rows 1-3 and 7-9. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs)* The cadence tests are `e mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0` (IA-14 rows 4 to 6), and invariant I-1 (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0`; legal `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS` values 1, 2, 3 and 6) makes every block end a check tick, so no step is credited on an unlit or out-of-reach block end. The hook is `after: emitter.place`, so it reads tick T's table, not T−1's. *Decides:* R10, EM-25, the Controller's own flag at PCI:677 ("Interaction's rule to confirm" — confirmed).
148

221	| 9 | `e == D − resume_offset` | completion: resolve to `DONE` or an outcome (D.3), publish through owner state change (KRN:96), clear `channel_ref` through the Controller mutator *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: this is also the only tick on which `record_falsification` is called for a `field_check` (IA-30) and the only terminal state that may release a RESERVED FULL-job part, on `OUTCOME` (IA-18); every abort row 1 to 6, `cancel_channel` and a restore instead commit or release the reservation by the blocks-credited rule of IA-18)*; for a record whose `owner_system` is not INTERACTION (Assembly's weld and seam cut) Interaction applies nothing at DONE but the `channel_ref` clear and the ledger delete, and exposes the DONE handoff `(seat, owner_system, verb_id, target_ref)` in `channel_view` for that tick (IA-35) |
222	
223	Properties (each is an acceptance row): (a) the lit check at `e = 0` re-reads tick T after `validate` read T−1, so a lamp that died in between aborts at progress 0; (b) a lamp that dies at `e = 6j + 1` lets ticks `6j + 1 … 6j + 5` accrue (**five dark ticks at most**, matching Emitter State AC-59b), and the check at `e = 6j + 6` aborts *before* block `j + 1` is credited, so no step and no ledger credit is ever earned on an unlit block end; (c) a lamp that flickers off and on again inside one block costs nothing and the block is credited; (d) a move on `e = D` leaves `blocks_done = n − 1` (PC-7: "one tick short" — the move wins); (e) steps land at `Tb + 6, Tb + 12, …`, never on `Tb`; (f) rows 4 to 6 test `e mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0`, not `e mod B`, and invariant I-1 (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0`) makes every block end a check tick, so no step is credited on an unlit or out-of-reach block end under any legal retune of `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS`. **The Graph-read lag, stated and not hidden:** the Graph's three hooks run on `T mod 6 == 0` (power), `2` (atmo) and `4` (failure) (Graph LS-8), and each runs *before* `interaction.step` on its tick (through the `emitter.place` chain). A step applied at tick `Tb + 6j` is read by the hook that consumes that mutator's effect on the first of its ticks strictly after the apply: hp changes (M7/M8/M10-class) by the failure hook (phases 8-9, `T mod 6 == 4`), requests and loads (M14, M13 valve/breaker) by the power hook (phases 0-2, `T mod 6 == 0`). The lag is the distance to the next such tick, 1 to 6 ticks in every case (≤ 100 ms); the range is unchanged. "The hiss stops when hp crosses `LEAK_HP`" therefore trails the step by up to one Graph step; this is the honest timing. *Alternative considered:* steps only on the failure-hook tick (`T mod 6 == 4`) — removes the lag variance but makes the effective duration 180 to 185 ticks and the bar length depend on the begin offset (rejected). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: the former derivation assumed the three Graph hooks share `T mod 6 == 0`; under the Graph's baseline stagger, offsets 0/2/4, they do not. Recomputed: the [1, 6] tick range is unchanged.)* A channel never locks movement; the facing locks during a channel (Controller behaviour, `FACING_HYSTERESIS`). A pause does not interrupt a channel — the tick simply does not advance (CR-16). *Decides:* R9, R10, L46 (PC-7), EM-25, R4.
224	
225	**IA-15 Abort causes, cues, no buffering.** The closed set of abort causes: `MOVED`, `CANCELLED`, `UNLIT`, `OUT_OF_REACH`, `TARGET_GONE`, `BODY` (stagger, downed, body transfer, seat rebind — the sub-cause is diagnostic), `NOT_ELIGIBLE`, `RESTORE`. A channel record ends in exactly one terminal state: `DONE`, `ABORT(cause)` or `OUTCOME(sub)` (IA-12); when `cancel_channel` and an abort cause fall on the same tick, `cancel_channel` (P2) wins and the hook finds no record. A `cancel_channel` with no channel is **Applied as a no-op** (counted `IA_CANCEL_NOOP`), not rejected: the Adapter sends `cancel` on every hold release, and a reject there would play the dull "no" cue after every completed channel. Cues are specified in Visual/Audio Requirements and Game Feel; their *meaning* is fixed here: cancel (the player let go) drains the bar; abort (the world or the body ended it) snaps the bar empty with a distinct "interrupted" cue; completion fills it; a deferred outcome fills it and then plays "nothing happened"; an immediate rejection withdraws the acknowledgement within one frame with a dull cue and no shake *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the withdrawal alone is sub-perceptible, and a mashed press could flicker it faster than the 3 Hz ceiling. The HUD therefore holds the restored keycap in a one-step Graphite-lit state for `BAR_REJECT_HOLD_TICKS` (HUD-owned, proposed 9, safe range 6 to 18) and admits at most one reject presentation per seat per `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS`; the rejection stays a cut and a cue, never a shake)*. "Stopped", "interrupted" and "nothing happened" are three different sounds and three different shapes. `ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS` is 0: a press during a channel is submitted and answered `BUSY`; nothing queues for "after" (PCI:84). The abort cause is delivered to presentation as diagnostic data only and the HUD never reads it; the one bit the HUD needs, the player's own cancel versus every world cause, is the non-diagnostic `channel_view.ended_by` (IA-41): one drain for `PLAYER_CANCEL`, one abort frame set and one abort cue for every `WORLD` cause (HUD & Suit Layer OQ-HS-19). *Decides:* L47, L49, R10.
226	
227	**IA-16 Partial progress.** *Incremental repair needs no ledger* (advisor R9): an abort leaves hp physically raised by the steps already applied, which is honest. **Non-incremental channels** (`begin_cut`, `begin_cap`, `begin_crank`, `field_check`, `begin_revive`, and Assembly's `begin_weld` and `begin_seam_cut`, whose records are Interaction's, IA-35) write a ledger entry on abort keyed `(seat, subject_ref, verb_id)` = `{blocks_done, abort_tick, n}` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `n` added so a retuned duration discards the entry, D.6; **`begin_harm` is removed from this list, delegated G2 following the creative-director's BLOCKING reading of the D36 ruling**: a harm re-begin always restarts at `e = 0` with its own full escape window, because the cumulative damage already persists in the victim's Suit integrity and a resumed bar would put the next damage 6 ticks after the re-begin, defeating the 65-tick walking window that D36 guarantees)*. A re-begin by the same seat on the same subject and verb with `T − abort_tick ≤ PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` (inclusive) resumes: `resume_offset = blocks_done × B`, the remaining time is `(n − blocks_done) × B` ticks, and the bar continues from `blocks_done / n` (the bar is a function of declared duration and the player's own history, never of any module-body field, IA-11c). After `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` the entry is gone; it is also deleted on `DONE` or an outcome. The ledger is bounded by `MAX_PARTIAL_ENTRIES` per seat; when full, the entry with the smallest `abort_tick` is evicted (ties: the smallest `subject_ref`); expiry is evaluated every tick in the hook so snapshot contents are replay-stable. The ledger ages on global ticks whatever the subject's section is doing: an entry on a dormant derelict's subject expires `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` after its abort like any other, so a partial cut never survives a hop leg (600 ticks against a 945-tick leg; Boarding ASK-BS-I5). A `BODY` abort still credits finished blocks. Noise is pushed only for newly accrued ticks, so splitting a job does not reduce its total noise, only spreads it. *Why a short TTL:* no persistence punishes a cancel-to-peek, which is the Pillar 2 behaviour "I can leave now"; permanent persistence is a free ratchet for splitting a noise burst; proportional decay is more state for no gain. *Constraint on a neighbour:* splitting a job reduces peak Attention only if the gap is comparable to Attention's noise memory `TAU_ATT_TICKS` (1800, registry); `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS ≤ 2 × TAU_ATT_TICKS` is accepted by Attention (registry `noise_unit_relations` IR-3; Attention System, Designed — AT-3). *For incremental repair hp is the ledger:* a re-begin recomputes D.1 from the then-current hp over the full block count, so the work already applied is kept and the only loss on a one-tick-short abort is a fresh bar for the last block's basis points (a block-granular ledger for repair was proposed and rejected at the checkpoint: a second record of the same quantity could disagree with hp after M7 clamps, decay, `apply_damage` or another seat's repair). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **a restore writes no ledger entry.** `post_restore` drops the in-progress channel as `ABORT(RESTORE)` for presentation purposes only; it neither creates a partial-progress entry from the dropped record nor refreshes `abort_tick` of an existing one, so a save-restore cycle can neither start nor extend a resume window; entries that survived the snapshot keep their absolute `abort_tick` and age on global ticks as before. The one persisted record a restore does touch is the FULL-job part record, which commits or releases by the blocks-credited rule (IA-18); that is a part-stock transition, not a ledger entry. The honest cost of leaving, restated for the Player Fantasy: hp already raised stays; a cut, cap, crank or field check resumes only within `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`; a resumed PATCH recomputes over the full bar.)* *Decides:* R9, PCI Open Question 7.
228	
229	**Group D — Repair, the part, and the patch**
230	
231	**IA-17 Repair is real, incremental `repair_step`.** For `begin_patch` the hook, at every credited block (IA-14 row 8), calls `check_repair_step` and then M7 `repair_step(subject_kind, id, delta_bp, kind)` with `delta_bp` = `repair_step_delta` (D.1). `hp_at_begin` is read in the hook at the first step, never in `validate` (IA-11a). **Healthy-subject guard (Interaction's own, independent of the Graph's answer to the hp-clamp question):** the hook never calls M7 PATCH when `hp_at_begin ≥ LEAK_HP` **and** `cap_at_begin > PATCH_CAP_BP` (the subject has never been patched and nothing is leaking), and never calls M7 at all when `repair_step_delta ≤ 0`; such a job runs its full duration with zero mutator calls and resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING, delegated G2 (the creative-director's Option B): the former threshold, `hp_at_begin` at or above the patch cap itself, left the silent band open: at true hp 4000 to 5999 a PATCH gained at most 1999 bp, permanently lowered `hp_cap` by 4000 bp and emitted the Graph's patch weep, which a healthy pipe does not, so a one-block tap-and-cancel probed a pipe's true state at the price of a block, the P4 failure Design Test 2 names. The guard is now keyed on the real harm: **both** `hp_at_begin` and `cap_at_begin` are read in the hook at the first step (the Graph's `node()` / `edge()` carry `hp_cap`, as M6's `SalvageRecord` does). A PATCH on a subject that is not leaking and has never been patched is "not a job a patch can do": silent damage is FULL work (Pillar 5), and the job runs the full bar and resolves `NOTHING_TO_REPAIR` identically at hp 10000, 5999, 5000 and 4000 with `hp_cap` 10000, with identical Graph state, descriptors and noise. Resume and top-up are kept: a half-patched subject has `hp_cap` = `PATCH_CAP_BP`, so the guard does not fire and the job continues (AC-IA-15, AC-IA-27, AC-IA-143, D.1 example 5). Leaking subjects (hp below `LEAK_HP`) are patched as before: their cold and hiss already tell the player. The Graph-side cure (M7 PATCH never lowers `hp_cap`, no weep before completion) stays open for the Graph owner (Open Question 10) and would make the guard a pure optimisation.)* A Graph answer `ABOVE_PATCH_CAP`, if M7 ever returns one, maps at the end of the bar to `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` as well (D.3), never to a distinct token. *Why:* otherwise a hallucinated-broken healthy pipe (hp `HP_FULL`) would have its `hp_cap` written down to `PATCH_CAP_BP` by LS-23 and go permanently DEGRADED — a hallucination physically damaging a module, breaking Pillars 1 and 4 together. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; **superseded by the re-review amendment above, which moves the guard to `LEAK_HP` and `cap_at_begin`**: the `PATCH_CAP_BP` threshold of the guard is arbitrary, and its residual is wider than "1 bp for a cap write". A hallucinated-broken pipe whose true hp lies in 4000 to 5999 is silent (no leak, because `hp ≥ LEAK_HP`), so no consequence channel warns the player, and a PATCH on it raises hp by at most 1999 bp while permanently writing `hp_cap` from 10000 down to 6000, a loss of 4000 bp of ceiling. The preferred cure is the Graph's: **M7 PATCH never lowers `hp_cap`** (it only ever raises `hp`, up to `min(hp_cap, PATCH_CAP_BP)`), which makes the guard a pure optimisation; this is routed to the Graph owner and must be answered before the repair story (Open Question 10). The interim recording of the damage range in Edge Cases B and AC-IA-90 is replaced by the guard.)* A hallucinated-fixed pipe at true hp 2000 receives real increments against 2000; its cold and its hiss persist until true hp crosses `LEAK_HP` (LS-22). A DESTROYED subject is never repairable (LS-23): the first `check_repair_step` fails, zero mutator calls, the job runs its full duration and resolves `PRECONDITION(NOT_REPAIRABLE)`. **Class A calls from a P3 hook are legal:** LSG:176 ("callable only inside a kernel-issued `WriteScope` in P2/P3") and LSG:186 (M7's caller is "Interaction (`begin_patch` channel steps)") both say so, and kernel CR-9 (KRN:104: a hook uses a published unconditional mutator or a SYSTEM-origin command) is satisfied because every step is check-then-apply: the check precedes the apply, a failing check skips the apply, and `apply` therefore stays infallible and is never FAULTED. A reader of CR-9 alone may object; both citations are given here for that reason. **The self-patch (object class ACTOR_SELF; Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-22 / SE-40).** A declaration row of object class ACTOR_SELF (welder in hand, CHANNEL, `PATCH_CHANNEL_TICKS`, noise TOOL, payload `{target_ref}` = the actor's own PlayerId) lets the actor patch their own suit. Its incremental steps run at the IA-14 cadence and call Suit's `patch_integrity(actor, delta)` with `delta` from D.1 evaluated against `SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP` (Suit's symbol, cited, never restated) and `integrity_bp` read **in the hook**, never in `validate`; the same healthy-subject guard applies (no call when `integrity_bp` already meets the cap; the job resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)`). There is no part and no FULL variant at MVP. The actor's own body is the honest actor channel, so reading `integrity_bp` is not an oracle question. The self-patch is an `act_gate`-exempt actor verb (IA-6): lamp on or off, with no other light, the press is accepted and the channel is not aborted `UNLIT`. *Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6 (GAP; the Controller's PC-6 option (a) is the spec; Emitter State's EM-21 rule that the owner's beam adds nothing to the owner's `act_lux_pm` stays intact, option (b) is not taken).* The self-patch story is no longer blocked. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs. Replaces the 2026-10-27 routed acceptance condition and the design-review note that blocked the story.)* MVP if and only if Suit's integrity axis is MVP (SE-22 lists MVP damage sources, so it is). *Decides:* R4, R9, LS-18, LS-22, LS-23, Suit SE-22.
232	
233	**IA-18 PATCH versus FULL, the part reservation, and the Item DB's AC-40 statements.** FULL if and only if the actor holds `parts_per_full` of `repair_part_for(subject_kind, kind_id, loop)` (`repair_part_for` cited by registry name, `parts_per_full` by the Item DB's own name; neither restated), or already holds a PAID record for the subject (a RESERVED record exists only while that seat's channel runs); otherwise PATCH. The choice is made in `validate` from the actor's own stock (the honest actor channel), so the channel's duration never depends on hp. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the stock rule above removes a decision. Whenever a part is stowed FULL is selected automatically, so a player cannot spend a cheap patch on a minor leak and keep the deep-derelict part for a real repair; that removes the Pillar 5 resource choice and fails Autonomy (SDT). **The selector is the actor's declaration, not their stock:** FULL if and only if the actor holds `parts_per_full` of the part **and has it readied** in Suit's hand rail (`part_ready(player_id, def_id)`, the actor's own selection, read in `validate`; reuses the IA-5 idea of "what is in hand"; a read of the actor's own state, never of hp, so it is no oracle), or already holds a PAID record for the subject; otherwise PATCH. A player holding the part who has not readied it completes a PATCH with the part untouched (AC-IA-135). The false claim that the bar class is "visible before the press" is withdrawn from Game Feel: `focus_view.duration_class` shows LONG pre-press only to a player who readied the part, which is their own choice told back to them, and nothing else on the plate shows the length class before the press. **Provisional on Suit:** `part_ready` and the hand-rail readying are a Suit ask (Open Question 42, cross-GDD note). Until Suit answers, the stock rule above stays in force as an interim and the autonomy defect stays open, labelled.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated G2 (creative-director: this undermines Pillar 5 more than any number): **the MVP selector is chosen, and there is one: the stock rule, with a mandatory pre-press tell.** The `part_ready` selector above is **not** an MVP rule: it rests on a Suit API that does not exist (the selector was "provisional on Suit" while IA-41, D.13 and AC-IA-91 already read it as fact), so two selectors lived in the same document. At MVP: FULL iff the actor's own stock holds `parts_per_full` of `repair_part_for(subject_kind, kind_id, loop)` or a PAID record exists, else PATCH; the commit at 100 ms is no longer an ambush because `focus_view` carries `part_tell` (IA-41), a bool true iff the focused V1 subject's declared kind has a repair part (`repair_part_for` not NONE) and the actor's own stowed count meets `parts_per_full`, drawn as a second notch on the keycap with no colour, numeral or pip (form proposed, HUD & Suit Layer owns the asset). It is a function of the declared kind and the actor's own stock only, never of hp or module-body state, so it is no oracle. A player who does not want to spend the part on this subject has the whole pre-press window to look elsewhere; a press that commits inside the first `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` costs nothing, and the Game Feel text now says exactly that. The `part_ready` / hand-rail selector stays the Suit ask of Open Question 42 as a **post-MVP upgrade** that would give the player an explicit choice; where it lands it replaces the stock rule and the tell changes meaning to "readied". Every "readied" in IA-41, D.13, AC-IA-91 and AC-IA-135 is therefore the post-MVP form, marked as such.)* The following statements discharge Item DB AC-40 and are normative:
234	1. `repair_part_for` returning `NONE` means **no FULL job is ever offered** on that subject (PATCH only); there is no `BLOCKED` for a missing part — FULL is simply not offered without it. (A SEAM subject returns `NONE`; a seam is restored by V9 re-weld.)
235	2. **A PATCH consumes no item.**
236	3. A FULL job issues only `kind = FULL` steps (IDB AC-38); a job never mixes kinds.
237	4. **A seat's part is spent when that seat's first productive step is applied** — a step that raises `hp` or raises `hp_cap` — through Suit's `consume_reserved` (Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-41). A whole subject costs time and no part if no step is ever productive. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: restated by the commit rule below. A part is spent at the first productive step, or, if no step was productive, when the channel ends by cancel, abort or restore after at least one block was credited; it comes back only when the bar runs to its end with no productive step. "Costs time and no part" therefore holds only for a bar that runs to the end.)*
238	5. A FULL job interrupted after its first productive step keeps the part spent and the hp; there is no refund (IDB AC-38). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the same holds for a job interrupted after its first credited block, productive or not, so that the two truth branches cannot be told apart by what the interruption returns.)*
239	6. A FULL job re-issued by **the same seat on the same subject** within `FULL_JOB_GRACE_S` (Interaction's own constant, 60 s [PLACEHOLDER], carrying the Item DB's resume-allowance recommendation) is not charged again; other seats are charged. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the grace is measured from the last credited block of the interrupted job, not from the last productive step, so its length does not depend on module-body state.)*
240	7. A FULL job on a subject already at `hp_cap = HP_FULL` with `hp = hp_cap` consumes nothing and resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` as an Applied-and-did-nothing outcome *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: only if the bar runs to its end; cancelled after a credited block it consumes the part exactly as it would on a damaged subject)*.

content.content:
241	8. PATCH on a subject that is not leaking (`hp ≥ LEAK_HP`) and has never been patched (`hp_cap > PATCH_CAP_BP`): the prompt still appears (IA-11b); the job resolves `NOTHING_TO_REPAIR` unless the actor holds the part, in which case it is a FULL job — the Item DB's "offer only FULL there" reading is adopted as behaviour, and the hp-clamp question stays routed to the Graph owner. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING: was "a subject whose `hp` already exceeds `PATCH_CAP_BP`"; the guard of IA-17 is keyed on the real harm.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "holds the part" reads "has the part readied" under the declaration selector above.)*
242	9. DESTROYED is never repairable (IA-17): the path is salvage (scrap) then install.
243	
244	**Part reservation and the commit rule (closes an oracle; orchestrator ruling, rewritten by the design review).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review, BLOCKING: the former reservation released the part at `until = Tb + FULL_CHANNEL_TICKS` whatever the player did, so a player could press a FULL job, cancel at e = 7 to 10, walk away and read the pack at `until`: the part returned only if the module was truly healthy (a hallucination). That is a lie detector priced at "time and a held resource" the player pays while standing nowhere near the pipe, not lit, not loud, so its Pillar 3 and Pillar 4 price (exposure plus TOOL noise) was about 2 to 3 % of the channel's, and the former Edge Case and AC-IA-30 pinned the leak as correct. The creative-director ruling, game-designer's form, replaces it: the reservation outcome is **branch-independent** from the first moment the two truth branches could differ.)*
245	
246	*Reservation.* When a FULL job is Applied, the part enters the state `RESERVED`. Suit treats a RESERVED or PAID part as having left the pack, in the stock count, in the carried mass that drives the weight cue and in its `reserved` bucket, **from the begin tick, in both truth branches** (SE-41). The record carries no timer: `until` is retired, and there is no expiry sweep.
247	
248	*The commit rule.* Let `blocks` be the number of blocks the channel has credited (IA-14 row 8). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `blocks` **is** the channel record's `blocks_done`, written by row 8 for FULL repair like every other verb, and `t_last_block` is the record's persisted field of the same name; a FULL job is never resumed through the ledger, so `blocks_done` is the run's own count.)* A block is credited in both truth branches whether or not its step was productive, so `blocks` is a branch-independent counter. The channel ends in exactly one terminal state, and the part record resolves with it:
249	1. **`DONE`.** The part was consumed at the first productive step (statement 4, `consume_reserved`); the record is `PAID(grace_until)` until the same hook run's completion closes it (NONE; the job is finished, so there is nothing left to resume) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: PAID is closed by the `DONE` event itself, never by a test of hp, see Re-begin below)*.
250	2. **`OUTCOME`** (the bar ran to its end and no step was productive: `NOTHING_TO_REPAIR`, `NOT_REPAIRABLE`). **This is the only path that returns a part:** `release_stowed`, the record becomes NONE. The `NOTHING_TO_REPAIR` outcome is the deferred reveal, paid for with the full bar.
251	3. **`cancel_channel`, any `ABORT(cause)` (`MOVED`, `UNLIT`, `OUT_OF_REACH`, `TARGET_GONE`, `BODY`, `NOT_ELIGIBLE`) or a restore** (a restore drops the channel as `ABORT(RESTORE)`, IA-36):
252	   - **`blocks = 0`** (the channel ended before its first block was credited): no step has been applied in either branch, the two branches are identical, and the part is released at once in both (`release_stowed`, record NONE).
253	   - **`blocks ≥ 1`**: the part is consumed **in both truth branches** (`consume_reserved` if it is still RESERVED; already consumed if a productive step made it PAID) and the record is `PAID(grace_until)` with `grace_until = t_last_block + ticks_for_seconds(FULL_JOB_GRACE_S)`, `t_last_block` the tick of the last credited block. A truly healthy module and a truly damaged one therefore leave the stock, the weight cue and the reserved bucket identical at every tick after any cancel, abort or restore. Believing a lie and acting on it costs a part, and that is honest under P4.
254	
255	*What the player can still learn, and what it costs.* Pressing a FULL job and letting the bar run to its end tells the truth (a part comes back, or it does not): the whole bar, lit, stationary and loud. Cancelling before the first block (`e < GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`) tells nothing and costs nothing, because nothing has differed. Cancelling at any later tick tells nothing and costs the part. The cheap checks stay the consequence channel and the scanner (IA-30).
256	
257	*Re-begin.* A re-begin by the same seat on the same subject while a PAID record exists is not charged again and issues only `kind = FULL` steps (statement 6); it reserves nothing. A RESERVED record exists only while a channel of that seat runs on the subject, so a re-begin never finds one. `grace_until` ends the record, as does the job completing or the subject being tombstoned or salvaged. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: **"completing" is the channel's `DONE` event, never a predicate sweep.** The former parenthesis, `hp = hp_cap = HP_FULL`, could be read as a per-tick test, under which a truly healthy module's PAID record would die the tick after it is created and a re-begin would charge a second part: a stock oracle (healthy and damaged modules would then differ at the re-begin). The record is deleted only by `grace_until`, by the `DONE` event of the FULL channel that closes a damaged subject, or by tombstone/salvage; it is not deleted by anything that reads hp. The loaded-set figures stay as Derelict Authoring's registered upper bound. At S4 the loaded `S_total` = 145 + 24 + 4 + 2 = 175 ≤ `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` 192 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Derelict Authoring L_seed B 3, one loose placement fewer)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*, so nothing fails dark, and no nearest-subject cull exists; "resolved by proximity" in Boarding ASK-BS-I5 (d) means focus, not registration.)* **Registration window (D37, user ruling: register subjects by body adjacency or proximity, not by loaded section).** `sync_section` still runs at the same callers and now maintains only the section's **candidate table** (declared interactables from Layout's `subject_anchors`, the loose items placed in it, its stubs: data, not Emitter subjects); a candidate becomes a subject (Emitter `register_subject`, E6) only while it is inside the **registration window** `W` of a bound body: the rooms (`room_id`, from `subject_anchors`) whose hop distance from a bound body's current room is at most `SUBJECT_WINDOW_HOPS` ([PLACEHOLDER — derive at spike], provisional 2), a hop being one door, seam hatch or dock link, counted across welded seams and docks. The hook recomputes `W` only when a bound body's `room_id` changes and on restore, section instantiate, discard and dormancy, at most once per tick, in room-id order; a candidate registers on entering `W` and unregisters when its room is beyond `SUBJECT_WINDOW_HOPS + 1` (a one-hop hysteresis, so a body standing on a threshold never flaps). Items the player creates (drops, salvage yield) sit at the player's feet and so are always in `W`. A subject outside `W` is unregistered and answers exactly as an unlit one (EM-21), which is correct because `in_reach` cannot be true for it; AC-IA-144 asserts that every candidate in reach from every walkable foot position is in `W`. `W` is a function of body positions, a SIM fact, so it is deterministic; `post_restore` rebuilds it from the restored positions, reading the restored `pos_curr` of `body.state` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, and persists no new state. **The budget is re-scoped** to the window: `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` 120 and `PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE` 24 keep their values and the I-7 relation, and the lint is `W_int(p) = F + L_seed + C` summed over the rooms of `W` and its hysteresis ring (hop distance up to `SUBJECT_WINDOW_HOPS + 1`), at most `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` at every authored body position `p` of each registered loaded set (D.10). Because a window is a subset of its loaded set, `S_int` of `legal_loaded_sets` (70 / 102 / 113 / 113 / 145) is an upper bound on `W_int`: S0 to S3 pass by construction (113 ≤ 120), S4 passes iff every window excludes at least 25 of its 145 subjects, and the runtime total never exceeds the loaded sum (175 ≤ 192) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Derelict Authoring L_seed B 3, one loose placement fewer)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* The S4 verdict depends on room-level subject counts that Derelict Authoring and Layout own, so it is measured, not assumed ([PLACEHOLDER — derive at spike]). A runtime overflow (E6 returns false and the object fails dark, which reads as a hallucination) is a content defect, counted `IA_SUBJECT_OVERFLOW`, never a gameplay state. A `drop` or `place_loose` needs a headroom read from Emitter State (provisional name `subject_headroom()`); a player `drop` with no headroom is refused `OBSTRUCTED`, so a dropped item can never be left unregistered and un-pickable. 350	### States and Transitions
351	
352	*Interaction holds no per-object state of its own beyond the records below: the objects' own states (hp, positions, stocks) belong to the Graph, Emitter State, the Item DB and Suit. Every transition here is caused by a command applied in P2, by `interaction.step` in P3, or by `post_restore`; presentation never causes one. `ACK` is not a simulation state — it exists only in the Adapter's pre-play between the press and the result event (PCI:84, 86).*
353

358	| NONE | no record | CONFIRMED on a verb's apply | — | `IDLE`; the Adapter shows `ACK` between press and result |
359	| CONFIRMED | the verb's `apply` (P2) created the record at `e = 0`, `progress` 0 | PROGRESS on the same tick's hook run (`e ≥ 1` accrues); ABORT at `e = 0` rows 1 to 6; `ABORT(CANCELLED)` if cancelled in P2 of a later tick | the seat's PLAYER command; the Controller mutator `set_channel_ref` runs in the same apply | `CONFIRMED`; identical for a command that will later resolve to an outcome (IA-12) |
360	| PROGRESS | `e ≥ 1` accrued | PROGRESS each tick; DONE; ABORT(cause); OUTCOME(sub) | the hook only | `PROGRESS`, `progress_pm = floor(progress × 1000 / D)`; steps at every `e mod B == 0` |

504	## Formulas
505	
506	*Conventions.* Everything hashed or replicated is integer-only (kernel determinism rule, D.10 and D.12 of the kernel); `ceil(a / b)` is `(a + b - 1) div b` for positive `b`; the only fixed-point scale is the Controller's 1/256 direction scale. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: **`floor` in this section means `floori`, and wherever a numerator can be negative (D.1, D.1b, D.8) the operand is clamped to be non-negative first;** GDScript `/` on integers truncates toward zero, which differs from a floor for a negative numerator, and the project lints `INTEGER_DIVISION`.)* `B` is `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` (6); `Tb` is the tick whose P2 applied a begin command; `e = T - Tb`. Upstream formulas are cited by registry name (`in_reach`, `lit(ref)` hysteresis, `fairness_gate`, `repair_part_for`, `salvage_yield`), never restated. **Id index (the ids are cited by Core Rules and must not shift; "Controller D.9 / D.10" and "Pipeline" references always carry their owner's prefix):** D.1 `repair_step_delta` · D.2 `act_gate` · D.3 `channel_outcome` · D.4 `throw_landing` · D.5 `drop_placement` · D.6 `partial_resume` · D.7 `full_job_charge` · D.8 `harm_step` · D.9 `noise_push` · D.10 `subject_budget` · D.11 `channel_clock` · D.12 `door_attempt` · D.13 `length_class`. (Orchestrator ruling: D.7, D.9, D.10, D.12 and D.13 fill ids that Core Rules did not cite, so no citation moved.)
507	
508	### D.1 repair_step_delta
509	
510	The repair_step_delta formula is defined as:
511	
512	`delta = ceil((target_cap - hp_at_begin) / n)`, applied once per credited block through `check_repair_step` then M7; **skipped (zero mutator calls)** when `hp_now >= target_cap` or `delta <= 0`.
513	
514	**Variables:**
515	
516	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
517	|---|---|---|---|---|
518	| `hp_at_begin` | int bp | 0..`HP_FULL` | the Graph's true `hp`, read **in the hook** at the first step of this run (e = `B`), never in `validate` (IA-11a) | the subject's hp when this run's first step is credited |
519	| `target_cap` | int bp | `PATCH_CAP_BP` (PATCH), `HP_FULL` (FULL), `SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP` (self-patch, Suit's symbol) | registry / Suit | the ceiling this job raises hp towards |
520	| `n` | int | 30 (PATCH, self-patch), 60 (FULL) | `D / B` with `D` = `PATCH_CHANNEL_TICKS` or `FULL_CHANNEL_TICKS` | block count over the **full** declared duration (checkpoint CQ1: hp is the ledger, so a re-begin recomputes over the full `n`) |
521	| `hp_now` | int bp | 0..`HP_FULL` | the Graph, read in the hook | current hp, for the skip test |
522	| `kind` | enum | PATCH, FULL | IA-18, decided from the actor's own stock | passed to M7; a job never mixes kinds |
523	
524	**Output Range:** `delta` 1..200 for PATCH (hp 0), 1..167 for FULL (hp 0) at the default durations; never above 2 % of `HP_FULL` per block at the defaults. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: across the knob ranges `n` is 20..50 for PATCH (`PATCH_CHANNEL_TICKS` 120 to 300) and 40..100 for FULL (240 to 600), so `delta` reaches 300 for PATCH (3 %) and 250 for FULL (2.5 %); the "2 %" claim holds only at the defaults.)* M7 clamps any overshoot at `hp_cap`. An uninterrupted job gains exactly `target_cap - hp_at_begin`.
525	
526	**Example:** (1) PATCH on a leaking pipe at hp 3000: `delta = ceil(3000 / 30) = 100`; thirty steps at e = 6, 12, ... 180; hp reaches `LEAK_HP` 4000 at step 10 (e = 60) and 6000 at e = 180; the Graph reads the crossing at its next run (lag 1..6 ticks, IA-14). 611	The drop_placement formula is defined as:

613	`p0 = foot + round_q8(UNIT[facing] * DROP_OFFSET_PX)`; the result is `p0` if `free(p0)`, else the first `foot + STEP8[posmod(f - i, 8)] * TILE_PX` for `i = 0..7` (clockwise on screen, starting at the octant `f` nearest the facing) with `free(.)`, else `OBSTRUCTED`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: **STEP8 is now an explicit literal table**, indexed by the Controller's octant number, which counts counter-clockwise on screen from east (`aim_angle` 0 = east, 512 per octant, north = 1024; screen y points down): `STEP8[0] = (1, 0)` E, `[1] = (1, -1)` NE, `[2] = (0, -1)` N, `[3] = (-1, -1)` NW, `[4] = (-1, 0)` W, `[5] = (-1, 1)` SW, `[6] = (0, 1)` S, `[7] = (1, 1)` SE. 761	### D.12 door_attempt
762	
763	The door_attempt formula is defined as:
764	
765	`dir = OPEN if area_true == 0 else CLOSE` (fixed at apply); at `T == Tb + DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS`: if `served_pm == 0` -> `PRECONDITION(NO_POWER)`; else submit SYSTEM `set_opening {target_ref, area}` (`area = area_max` for OPEN, 0 for CLOSE); in P2 of T+1: if `dir == CLOSE` and `leaf_would_overlap(door_ref, 0, foot_boxes)` -> `CLOSING_BLOCKED` (the hook re-submits once, on the first clear tick of its pure read, *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was each tick*) else M13. A SYSTEM-origin close from a cascade takes the same P2 path with no window. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: four additions. (i) The attempt is keyed by `door_ref`, one per door for both faces. (ii) In the P2 apply, **if `area_true` already equals the target `area`, skip the check and M13 and end the attempt.** (iii) A PLAYER attempt that has spent `CLOSING_BLOCKED_TIMEOUT_TICKS` in `CLOSING_BLOCKED` ends with the leaf open and no token. 766	
767	**Variables:**
768	
769	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
770	|---|---|---|---|---|
771	| `area_true` | int | 0..`area_max` | the Graph's `opening(edge_id)` read (provisional), read in apply | the true leaf aperture |
772	| `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` | int ticks | 18..60 (default 30) | Interaction [PLACEHOLDER] | uniform window for powered and unpowered doors (no latency oracle) |
773	| `served_pm` | int pm | 0..1000 | the Graph, read in the hook only | motor power |
774	| `foot_boxes[]` | rect list | one per actor on the body, unfiltered (BDY-18) | Body's `foot_boxes(body_id)` (Ship Body & Interior Physics, Designed — BDY-18), read in the P2 apply of the SYSTEM `set_opening` (the boxes committed at the end of the previous tick) | passed to Layout's `leaf_would_overlap` (Layout, Designed — LY-11) |
775	
776	**Output Range:** exactly one of M13 applied (always in a P2 apply, never in P3), `PRECONDITION(NO_POWER)` (written by the hook, no command), or `CLOSING_BLOCKED` until clear; no outcome token exists for a late overlap. `TAP_REARM_TICKS` runs from the end of the attempt.
777	
778	**Example:** a PLAYER close at Tb = 500: the window ends at 530, the motor is powered, so the hook submits the SYSTEM `set_opening` at 530 and it applies at 531; a crewmate's foot box overlaps the leaf until it clears at 541: the attempt is `CLOSING_BLOCKED` from 531, the hook's pure read is clear first at 541 and it re-submits once there *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was "re-submitted each tick")*, and M13(0) lands in P2 of 542 (42 ticks after the press, the latch strain throughout and the motor sound only from the tick the leaf travels *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: was "the motor whine throughout")*), with `layout.doors` projecting the closed leaf in that same tick. Unpowered door: at 530 the hook sees `served_pm == 0`, the outcome is `PRECONDITION(NO_POWER)` and no command is submitted; the leaf never moved.

780	### D.13 length_class
781	
782	The length_class formula is defined as:
783	
784	`length_class = SHORT if mode == HOLD_CONFIRM; else MEDIUM if D < BAR_LONG_FROM_TICKS; else LONG`, computed per seat from (declaration row, tool, the actor's stock) and frozen at the press; for V1 it follows the PATCH/FULL choice of IA-18.
785	
786	**Variables:**
787	
788	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
789	|---|---|---|---|---|
790	| `D` | int ticks | 60..600 | D.11 | declared duration *(range corrected 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
791	| `BAR_LONG_FROM_TICKS` | int ticks | 180..300 (default 240) | Interaction [PLACEHOLDER] | MEDIUM/LONG boundary |
792	
793	**Output Range:** SHORT, MEDIUM or LONG; never a function of hp, state, `forced_mode` or `served_pm`.
794	
795	**Example:** patch (180) MEDIUM; FULL (360) LONG; crank and salvage cut (240) LONG; cap (90), field check (120), harm (204) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: derived from D36, was 120)*, revive (180) MEDIUM; V6 hold SHORT. 799	*Grouped by theme. Each case names its diagnostic counter where one exists (`IA_*`, owned by Interaction under `diag_panel_contract`). "Exact outcome" means the state the simulation is in afterwards; a presentation cue is named only where the cue is the specified outcome.*
800	
801	**A. Light, reach and the channel clock**
802	
803	- **If the lamp is off at a check tick (`e mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0`) mid-channel**: the channel ends `ABORT(UNLIT)`, the bar snaps empty with the *interrupted* cue, and the block ending on that tick is not credited (steps already applied stay applied; a non-incremental verb writes its ledger entry). `IA_CHANNEL_ABORT{UNLIT}`. No step is ever earned on an unlit block end (I-1). Not for the self-patch: an ACTOR_SELF record is `act_gate`-exempt (IA-6) and IA-14 rows 4-5 do not run for it *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs)*.
804	- **If the lamp flickers off and back on between two check ticks**: nothing aborts and the block is credited; at most `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS - 1` (5) dark ticks accrue. A flicker must not cancel work, and Emitter State AC-59b bounds the exposure.
805	- **If the lamp dies between `validate` (which read tick T-1's table) and the begin's `apply`**: the hook's check at `e = 0` re-reads tick T after `emitter.place` and aborts at progress 0 with no ledger entry. The one-tick staleness of `validate` can never start a job in the dark.
806	- **If a move intent is already held when `begin_*` is pressed**: `validate` answers immediate `BUSY` (PC-7: the owner requires `octant == NONE`; IA-10) and nothing is Applied. **If the move intent applies after `validate` within the same P2** (command order on one tick): the begin is Applied and the hook aborts `ABORT(MOVED)` at `e = 0` before any accrual; no step, no part use, no ledger entry (zero blocks). The move always wins (PC-7).
807	- **If the move intent arrives on the completion tick (`e = D`)**: abort-before-accrual leaves `blocks_done = n - 1`; a `begin_cut` module is not removed (M6 runs at completion only), a PATCH has landed 29 of 30 steps. The player re-begins; a cut resumes within `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`, repair recomputes from hp (D.1).
808	- **If the focused object sits exactly on the arc or distance rim at press**: `in_reach` decides in integers: at `d^2 = REACH_PX^2` it is in reach, one pixel beyond it is `OUT_OF_RANGE` (immediate, dull cue, no shake). `IA_REJECT{OUT_OF_RANGE}`. The prompt (HUD) may lag the rim by its show debounce but never leads it.
809	- **If `cancel_channel` and an abort cause fall on the same tick**: `cancel_channel` (P2) wins; one terminal state, the hook finds no record. If there is no channel at all, `cancel_channel` is Applied as a no-op (`IA_CANCEL_NOOP`) — the Adapter sends it on every hold release, and a reject would play the dull cue after every completed job.
810	- **If the pause is entered mid-channel**: the tick does not advance, so the hook does not run, nothing accrues, no TTL ages and no verb is admitted (`PAUSED`, never queued). Resuming continues from the same tick.
811	- **If the zoom step `k` or the HUD scale `H` changes mid-channel**: nothing in the simulation changes — `REACH_PX` and every Interaction length are base (world) pixels; only the HUD re-projects the plate and bar (UI Requirements).
812	- **If the player switches input device or uses hold versus toggle for the same verb**: the simulation sees the same command and the same `channel_view`; no Interaction rule reads the device (IA-4, lint). A pad user who never touches the right stick focuses by facing.
813	
814	**B. Repair, the part and the patch**
815	
816	- **If a PATCH targets a hallucinated-fixed pipe (true hp 2000)**: real increments land against 2000 (D.1: 134 bp per step), hp crosses `LEAK_HP` at step 15 (e = 90) and the hiss stops about 1.5 s into the job; no message appears. The cautious player is rewarded by physics (P1).

819	- **If a FULL job is interrupted after its first productive step (or, branch-independently, after its first credited block)**: the record is PAID, the part stays spent, hp stays raised, and a re-begin by the same seat within `FULL_JOB_GRACE_S` is not charged again and issues only `kind = FULL` steps. `IA_FULL_RESUME`. 821	- **If a FULL job is cancelled before its first block is credited (e < 6, or any abort at e = 0)**: `blocks` is 0, no step has differed between the branches, and the part is released at once in both (`IA_RESERVE_RELEASE`); the stock reads identically in both branches before and after.
822	- **If the same seat re-begins on a PAID record**: the record is reused, no second part is reserved or charged, and only `kind = FULL` steps are issued; a RESERVED record cannot be found by a re-begin because it exists only while a channel of that seat runs (IA-18).
823	- **If a FULL job's bar runs to its end on a module that never had a productive step**: the channel resolves `OUTCOME` (`NOTHING_TO_REPAIR` or `NOT_REPAIRABLE`) and the part returns (`IA_RESERVE_RELEASE`): the only path that returns a part after the first credited block.

The damage is real, silent and FULL work: the player who holds the part readied gets a FULL job there. A subject already patched (`hp_cap` = `PATCH_CAP_BP`) is topped up or resumed normally. Pinned by AC-IA-90 and AC-IA-26.

1073	## Game Feel
1074	
1075	*Units: 1 tick = 16.7 ms (`TICK_RATE` 60); a render frame at 60 Hz is one tick, at 30 Hz two. Every number is a design target for the Adapter, HUD and animation budget; the simulation values are the Formulas section's. No loop frame rate is invented here (ART 5.2 owns the work loop's 6 frames).*
1076	
1077	### Feel Reference
1078	
1079	**Borrow:** Project Zomboid's timed contextual actions: a linear bar, cancelled by moving, no skill-check minigame, and the hands-free chest lamp of *Pandorum* (the beam stays on the job while both hands work). The quality borrowed is deliberate, stationary, stiff competence under pressure: pressing is instant, the work takes visible time, and leaving is always free. **Anti-reference:** a Barotrauma-style repair minigame or any QTE (a UI surface that could leak module-body truth, and a rhythm demand the "I can leave now" test forbids), and circular or confirm-dialog action wheels (HR-14).

1123	### Weight and Responsiveness Profile
1124	
1125	*Weight:* heavy and deliberate in duration (3 to 6 s jobs), light in input (one press, no combo). *Player control:* total at every tick: nothing locks movement, nothing buffers (`ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS` 0), no QTE; the commitment is readable up front because the bar's length class is fixed by the declared verb and frozen at the press. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the "readable up front" claim holds for the part-consuming V1 job only through the mandatory pre-press tell `part_tell` (a second notch on the keycap, IA-41), derived from the actor's own stock; for every other verb the class is fixed by the declaration. Without the tell the claim is false under the MVP stock rule, and the tell is a HUD story precondition.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the former claim that "the part-stocked LONG variant is visible before the press" was false, since nothing pre-press showed LONG or the part consumption. It is withdrawn: under the ready-part declaration (IA-18) the LONG variant is the player's own choice, told back to them in `focus_view.duration_class`, and the plate shows no length pip; the first time a player sees the bar's length is the press.)* *Snap:* TAP and rejection are crisp and binary; channels are analog only in the stepped bar. *Acceleration:* the action starts instantly (ACK) and ends instantly (cut); there is no ramp-up or ease-out, so the player never wonders whether a press registered. *Failure texture:* fair and diegetic: a rejection never says why (no string, CR-5) but every immediate reason is something the player can see (out of reach, dark, busy, wrong tool); a deferred outcome costs the full bar, so the failure reads as "it wasn't really broken" or "it was still too hot", never "the game wouldn't let me".

1133	- [ ] The press-to-ack interval is imperceptible and a withdrawn ack never reads as a glitch (AC-IA-102).
1134	- [ ] Cancel, abort and nothing-happened are told apart with the sound off (AC-IA-100).

1154	**Rules the HUD GDD must meet.**
1155	- *Debounce and rate limit (D.UI-2, values *proposed* and owned by the HUD GDD).* `show = (prompt_state != HIDDEN) AND (stable_ticks >= PROMPT_SHOW_DEBOUNCE_TICKS 13) AND (since_last_show >= PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS 20)`; `hide = (prompt_state == HIDDEN) OR focus_ref changed`, immediately, same render frame, no dwell. Hide is immediate because a prompt for a subject that is not lit is a lie by commission; show may be late because a late prompt omits a hint. The limiter holds show-starts to 3 Hz as full cycles *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X9 / D91: the flash counting unit is `ceil(n_transitions / 2)`, the registry `flash_count`, i.e. full cycles, so `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` stays 20 and does not double; prompt show-starts are exempt from the per-area weighted `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` accounting as a creative-director exemption, and the strict ceiling is kept for the Alarm Red mark and under `reduce_flashing`, where this limiter is the strict 3 Hz cap)*. Worked cases: focus alternating every 6 ticks never shows; a fixture with `lit` period 12 never shows; period 30 shows at tick 13 of each on-phase at 3 Hz or slower. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` 0.10 (Controller) is the first defence, the debounce the safety net.
1156	- *Bar (D.UI-1).* `progress_pm = clamp(floor((T - begin_tick) x 1000 / duration_ticks), 0, 1000)`, `fill_px = floor(progress_pm x L / 1000)`; the only inputs are elapsed ticks, declared duration, `L`, and a resumed offset (the actor's own history). PATCH 180 ticks at `L` 24: `fill_px` 0, 6, 12, 24 at elapsed 0, 45, 90, 180. Never `hp`, `state`, `repair_step_delta` or `served_pm` (the identical-frame invariant I-UI-1; AC-IA-11, AC-IA-62).

If no result is seen within `PREPLAY_MAX_TICKS` 2 of `queued_tick`, withdraw as dropped (`UI_PREPLAY_TIMEOUT`); a late `Applied` re-creates the bar at the committed value. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `Applied`, `Rejected`, `Dropped` and `Superseded` are the `kind` of the result-event record, paired to the pre-play by `command_id` and `queued_tick`; the record carries no reason, so every `Rejected` plays the same frame set (IA-15).)*
1158	- *Cues from the transition counter.* Track `last_seen_transition_seq` per seat; play the terminal transition's cue; skip intermediate loops (Visual/Audio).
1159	- *Placement.* Plate position = projected anchor plus the AD-5 placement, snapped to the HUD art-px grid, held for as long as the same `focus_ref` is focused and re-validated only when invalid; none valid falls back to a clamped plate (`UI_PLACEMENT_FALLBACK`).
