content.thinking:
Wear ticks happen on absolute step_no multiples of 100, not relative to when the patch started decaying, so after the hold period ends, the first wear tick could land anywhere from 0 to 10 seconds later depending on the phase alignment.

For banked values of 4000, 5000, and 6000, I calculate the required number of wear ticks (1, 11, and 21 respectively) and derive time windows of roughly 240–250s, 340–350s, and 440–450s — which matches the "about 250/340/440" language in the spec, but a precise test should assert the full interval rather than a single point, since the exact timing depends on step phase.

I also need to check whether patched_at_step gets overwritten on every PATCH call or only set once, since this determines when the 240s hold actually begins — if M7 updates it on each step, the hold starts from the last step, which matters for cancelled patches too. There's also a question about whether duty wear from running machines stacks with the base wear rate during a patch, though that seems not to apply to pipes since they lack duty wear.

Testing a cancellation at hp 3500 (below LEAK_HP) with the segment formula gives a negative numerator, but truncating division versus floor division both land on the same clamped result of 1, so that edge case resolves consistently regardless of which integer division convention is used.

I notice the formula really should be written with an explicit max(0, h−LEAK_HP) rather than relying on the division behaving correctly, and the stated range of h 4000..6000 for a patched subject is actually wrong — a cancel before step 10 can leave h anywhere from 3001 to 3999, meaning the patch plate exists but the pipe is still leaking. That's a real documentation gap worth flagging as a minor recommendation.

Now I'm moving on to review Open Questions 1504-1617.

### D.17 Reachable-set subject budget

The `subject_budget_per_set` formula is defined as:

`S_int(S) = F(S) + L_seed(S) + C` ; `S_total(S) = S_int(S) + PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE + ACTORS + HORRORS` ; `SUBJECT_BUDGET_SET iff S_int(S) > INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET or S_total(S) > MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` ; `I-7: INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET + PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE <= floor(3 x MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS / 4)` ; `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS_needed = ceil(4 x (INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET + PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE) / 3)`

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `F` | int | 0 to 120 | IA D.10 and IA-37; declared interactables (hardpoints, two face subjects per door, valves, hull segments, sockets) | Home 50 (48 + 2 scrubber slots, DA-47), A 28, B 40 |

| `C` | int | 0 to 18 | IA D.10 | Cap-stub worst case (at most 6 modules x 3 ports), counted once per set |
| `PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE`, `ACTORS`, `HORRORS` (Interaction's `P`, `A`, `H`) | int | 24, 4, 2 | IA D.10, I-7; registry `subject_budget` | 30 together; `H` is `HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 `[PLACEHOLDER: Horror]` Emitter HORROR subjects (one active plus one transient) |
| `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` | int | 120 `[PLACEHOLDER: Interaction]` | registry (Interaction-owned, IA-37) | Content ceiling for the per-registration-window sum `W_int(p) = F + L_seed + C` at every authored body position, not for `S_int` over a loaded set (registry `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET`, `subject_budget`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* |
| `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` | int | 192 `[PLACEHOLDER: Emitter]` (registry range 128 to 384) | registry (Emitter-owned) | Subject cap |

**Output Range:** `S_int` 70 to 145 and `S_total` 100 to 175 in MVP content as loaded-set sums (the design review's 68 to 143 and 98 to 173 plus the two scrubber slots of DA-47) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2: B carries three loose placements, so home 2, A 4, B 3)*.

findings.section: IA-37 / D.10 / I-7 / AC-IA-59 vs Derelict Authoring D.17 and registry legal_loaded_sets
findings.finding: IA-37 (L305), D.10 (L736-738) and Edge Cases F (L878) say that at S4 `S_total` = 145 + 24 + 4 + 2 = 175 <= 192, so 'nothing fails dark whatever the window'. That figure counts only authored F + L_seed + C. IA-37 itself registers INSTRUMENT and CONSOLE subjects through `subject_anchors` (kind_hint list, L305). IW-21 ships the inspect card live at MVP, so instruments are MVP content. Derelict Authoring D.17 (L1111-1122) computes the cumulative case: S4 with instruments (19) and consoles (4) is S_int 166 and `S_total` 196 > 192 (198 on the 145 base). The {home+B} neighbourhood is 130, over `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` 120 by 10. Interaction's 'runtime safety does not depend on the window' argument therefore fails once MVP instruments are authored. AC-IA-59 and AC-IA-144 would pass on the 70/102/113/113/145 figures while the real lint fails. The window radius is spike-gated, so this is not blocking, but the safety claim is stated as a guarantee.
findings.fix: State in IA-37, D.10 and AC-IA-59 that the 175/145 figures exclude INSTRUMENT (home 9, A 4-5, B 5) and CONSOLE (4) subjects. Add instruments and consoles to `F` (or to a named term) in D.10. Rewrite the runtime-safety sentence so it rests on the window lint at `SUBJECT_WINDOW_HOPS` (derive at spike) and not on 'window <= loaded sum <= 192'. Record that the D.17 cumulative case (S_total 196-198 > 192; {home+B} 130 > 120) is the spike's pass line, and route it to Derelict Authoring and Emitter State.

findings.section: IA-41 / UI Requirements / Cross-References row 1260 / AC-IA-64 / OQ 45 / registry input_view
findings.finding: G1 and R2 are not applied to the HUD read list. (a) Interaction still defines and names `input_view(seat) {hold_pm, armed, device_class, pressed_action}` (L313, L336, L1147, L1174, L1416, L1554). The Controller publishes `confirm_view = {b, mode, armed, pressed, released, give_up_live}` (player-controller L593, L881, AC-PCI-145). The HUD consumes `confirm_view` (hud L183). The registry keeps `input_view` only 'as the registered alias ... until Interaction and HUD conform', with source: still interaction-system.md although the owner is the Controller. (b) The result-event record is `{seat, command_id, queued_tick, kind}` (L313, L1152, L1157, L1416, AC-IA-139). `command_id` is not a kernel term. Kernel R2 stamps seq internally, keeps submit() void and echoes a caller-attached opaque `correlation` (kernel L87, L108, KRN-SEQ-05; player-controller L124 keys pre-play by it). AC-IA-64's allow-list lint (`hud_read_allowlist.json`) would reject a HUD built to the Controller and HUD GDDs.
findings.fix: Rename `input_view` to `confirm_view` in IA-41, UI Requirements, the Cross-References rows, AC-IA-64, OQ 45 and the Dependencies HUD row, and list the Controller's fields (b = hold_pm / 1000, mode, armed, pressed, released, give_up_live). Replace `command_id` with `correlation` in the result-event record and AC-IA-139. Ask the registrar to move the `input_view`/`confirm_view` source: to player-controller-input.md.

findings.section: IA-41 / Cross-References section 3 / OQ 49 vs HUD & Suit Layer; owed-refresh rows
findings.finding: HUD HS-41 (L286-299, L382) and its read-list row (L182) still map bar states to `channel_view.state` = IDLE, CONFIRMED, PROGRESS, ABORT, DONE, OUTCOME. They have no `last_result`/`prev_result` and no `part_tell` (grep returned 0 hits). Interaction restricted `state` to IDLE/CONFIRMED/PROGRESS and moved terminals to `last_result` (IA-41, AC-IA-61, AC-IA-131). A HUD built from the HUD GDD never sees a terminal and plays no DONE, ABORT or OUTCOME cue. G6 allowed the fix in the sibling; OQ 49(b) is still open. Separately, Cross-References section 3 still lists as 'owed' refreshes that have landed: the Controller's four mutators (row 1237; PCI L219 now documents set_channel_ref), the PC-8 door carve-out (row 1255), SL:276 (row 1245; save-load row 300 now lists interaction.state), and a Dependencies line that still calls the four mutator names 'proposed/provisional' (L303, L474, L893).
findings.fix: Route the HUD correction (terminals via last_result/prev_result, `part_tell` notch) to the HUD writer as a blocking precondition of the HUD bar story. Re-stamp the landed rows in section 3 and the Dependencies/Interactions tables as 'landed, verified <date>'. Drop 'proposed' from the Controller mutator names.

findings.section: IA-1 / IA-3 / IA-10 / Dependencies engine note vs kernel R3 (CR-19 callable contract)
findings.finding: The kernel's R3 contract (kernel L152-153): every kernel-invoked owner callable (validate, apply, step hooks, snapshot, restore, post_restore, read_view) takes `ctx` and its only return is `return ctx.complete()`, with results through ctx.ok()/ctx.reject(). Interaction never mentions it (grep for `ctx` and `complete()` returns nothing). IA-10 says `validate` 'returns the first of' the reasons, and engine item (1) (L918) speaks of 'typed validate()/apply()' handler bases. A story author following Interaction builds returning validates that the kernel treats as faulted. The prior pass listed this and it did not land.
findings.fix: Add one conformance sentence to IA-1/Conventions: all Interaction validate, apply, hook, read_view and restore callables follow kernel CR-19 (ctx, `return ctx.complete()`), and 'returns a reason' means ctx.reject(reason). Reword engine item (1) to the CompletionToken form. Add a lint row (L-CODE) that no Interaction callable returns anything but ctx.complete().

findings.section: AC-IA-110 vs IA-36 post_restore / States 8 / Save/Load REBASE_BLOCKS
findings.finding: AC-IA-110 (L1401) requires 'snapshot-restore-snapshot with every table populated is byte-identical'. IA-36 post_restore drops every in-progress channel (the persisted seat `channel{...}` record) and clears `last_result`/`prev_result` (L303, States 8 L439). A snapshot taken with a channel and a last_result populated cannot equal the post-restore snapshot. Save/Load puts interaction.state in REBASE_BLOCKS ('a restore normalisation, OQ-39', save-load L300). Interaction never mentions REBASE_BLOCKS, and its OQ 39 is an unrelated row, so the reference dangles. The row is untestable as written.
findings.fix: Rewrite AC-IA-110: 'byte-identical for ledger, full_jobs, throws, loose, stubs, last_salvage_T and counters; the seat channel record and last_result/prev_result are normalised by post_restore and compared under REBASED rules'. State in IA-36 that interaction.state is in Save/Load's REBASE_BLOCKS for exactly those fields. Fix the OQ reference.

findings.section: IA-41 press_blocked_moving / IA-10 BUSY / States 2 / AC-IA-142
findings.finding: `press_blocked_moving` is true on 'CHANNEL and HOLD_CONFIRM plates' (L324), with the stated meaning 'a `begin_*` press would be answered BUSY'. The BUSY-while-moving rule is on `begin_*` only (IA-10 L181; States 2 L371). V6 is a HOLD_CONFIRM `set_opening` and is not a `begin_*`. Nothing makes a V6 hold BUSY while moving, so the hollow-keycap tell on a V6 plate predicts a reject that does not occur. The tell must not lie. `field_check` is a CHANNEL verb with no `begin_` prefix, so the rule's wording leaves it unclassified (the hook abort at e = 0 covers the outcome). AC-IA-142 fixtures cover only CHANNEL and TAP.
findings.fix: Define the field by the declaration: true iff the row's mode is CHANNEL (every channel verb, `field_check` included, requires `intent_octant == NONE` at validate). Remove HOLD_CONFIRM from L324 and the HUD row, or state explicitly that a V6 hold is rejected BUSY while moving and add that to IA-10. Replace 'at a `begin_*`' with 'at a CHANNEL-mode verb' in IA-10 and AC-IA-18b. Add a V6 fixture to AC-IA-142.

findings.section: D.1b bead_segments / AC-IA-143 (auto half) / registry bead_segments
findings.finding: The re-leak times 'about 250 s, 340 s and 440 s' mix the upper bound of the first discrete window with the lower bounds of the others. Graph LS-23 and D.9: wear 100 bp lands only on `step_no mod WEAR_PERIOD_STEPS (100) = 0`, after a 2400-step hold, and LEAK returns when hp < 4000. From a banked h the number of wear ticks needed is floor((h - 4000)/100) + 1 = 1, 11, 21. The first tick falls 0.1-10 s after the hold, depending on phase. Windows: 4000 -> 240.1-250 s, 5000 -> 340.1-350 s, 6000 -> 440.1-450 s after the last PATCH step. 'About' cannot be asserted in an (auto) step. The variable table also says h is 4000..6000 for a patched subject. A patch cancelled before step 10 (hp 3001..3999, hp_cap already 6000) leaves h under LEAK_HP. The formula's clamp still returns 1, but the stated range is wrong and the D.1b header promises a non-negative operand clamp it does not show.
findings.fix: Rewrite the AC-IA-143 auto half: 'THEN the re-leak tick is the first wear tick (step_no multiple of 100) after patched_at_step + 2400 at which hp < LEAK_HP: within [240.1, 250] s, [340.1, 350] s and [440.1, 450] s of the last step'. Use the same windows in D.1b, Player Fantasy, OQ 41 and the registry output text. Write the formula as clamp(1 + floori(2 * max(0, h - LEAK_HP) / (PATCH_CAP_BP - LEAK_HP)), 1, 3) and widen the h range to 0..6000 with a note that h under 4000 gives one segment.

findings.section: Carried stale values (G3 sweep not completed): IA-3 table, IA-29, Tuning Knobs, registry, Quick reference
findings.finding: Leftovers the previous pass listed are still present. (1) IA-3 row `throw_glowstick` (L128) still says 'Q / R3'. Controller PC-2 and AC-PCI-129 say R3 is unbound and the binding is RB. IA-8 and IA-29 already say RB. (2) IA-29 (L287) says `THROW_RANGE_TILES` 3 (1 to 5). Tuning Knobs and D.4 say 3-5 (I-3), and registry THROW_RANGE_TILES still says 'range 1-5'. (3) Registry `channel_clock.expression` still has 'block j credited at e = B*j' (the retired absolute-j form; the GDD is the source, G1). (4) Tuning `BAR_LONG_FROM_TICKS` 180-300 (L954): at 180, PATCH (180 default, range up to 300) reads LONG, and the lint `HARM_CHANNEL_TICKS < BAR_LONG_FROM_TICKS` (204 by default, up to 240) forces a floor of at least 205 (241 at the harm range top), so the stated range is not jointly legal. (5) Quick reference (L20) still says Sanity '(undesigned)' and Attention '(undesigned, soft)'. Visual/Audio intro (L977) says the HUD GDD is 'undesigned'. Header 'Last Verified: 2026-10-26'. (6) States 2 (L371) and Edge Cases A (L806) say `validate` needs `octant == NONE`; IA-10 says `intent_octant`. (7) The split-halves list (L1476) still calls AC-IA-33b 'blocked on Emitter State'; L1493 says it is no longer conditional.
findings.fix: One G3 sweep: grep the old wording after each edit. Set L128 to RB. Set IA-29 to (3 to 5) and request the registry range 3-5. Update registry channel_clock to the j' / absolute j form. Set the BAR_LONG range to something that satisfies I-9 and the harm lint (for example 241-300), or add the joint lint to I-9. Fix the Quick reference, Visual/Audio intro, Last Verified, the `intent_octant` wording and the 33b note.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: untestable rows (quoted) with rewrites
findings.finding: Rows that a QA tester cannot execute as written. (a) AC-IA-143 auto: 'the Graph's re-leak times after completion are about 250 s, 340 s and 440 s'. (b) AC-IA-93: 'a grep of this GDD for PATCH_CAP_BP and PATCH_DECAY_S finds only the values 6000 and 240 (and the re-leak figures derived from them ...)'. It greps a design document, is self-referential, and the allowed hits change with every amendment. (c) AC-IA-102: 'the ACK frame appears within the same render frame' is tagged (manual) and the Game Feel line says 'imperceptible'. (d) AC-IA-124: 'no tester calls the press unresponsive, laggy or mushy' is keyword-based and has no n or threshold. (e) AC-IA-136b: 'perceived within about 10 s' has no clock. (f) AC-IA-12 'unreadable' is asserted by a spy, which is good, but 'unreadable ... before the terminal result_seq' is not stated against a tick.
findings.fix: (a) Use the wear-tick windows of the D.1b finding. (b) Replace with an L-DATA lint: `assets/data/interaction/` contains no key for PATCH_CAP_BP/PATCH_DECAY_S (values come from the registry), plus the registry referenced_by check; delete the GDD prose grep. (c) Make it (auto, HUD stub): input-event timestamp to first ACK frame <= 1 render frame at 60 and 30 Hz in the HUD double; keep a manual capture for the feel half. (d) Same 8-tester protocol as AC-IA-73b: at least 7 of 8 rate press responsiveness >= 4 of 5 on a post-session item, and zero logged 'unresponsive' episodes. (e) Pass iff the first Attention tell event occurs <= 600 ticks after the push in the build log, and 7 of 8 testers name it.

findings.section: Document hygiene: superseded text kept inline (IA-17, IA-18, IA-41, D.8, V-1..V-13, Cross-References row 1259-1267)

D.8 keeps struck-through examples. IA-41 carries three nested 'Amended' blocks. Stories are cut from this file behind a 40 KB read gate. A reader can still build the superseded selector or the old `input_view`.
findings.fix: Do a consolidation pass: fold each rule to its live statement, move superseded text to the Rulings appendix or the review log, and keep a single 'Amended <date>' marker per rule. Do it before epics are cut. This is the largest remaining defect-source risk.

Derelict Authoring D.17 (L1111-1122) computes the cumulative case: S4 with instruments (19) and consoles (4) is S_int 166 and `S_total` 196 > 192 (198 on the 145 base). The {home+B} neighbourhood is 130, over `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` 120 by 10. Interaction's 'runtime safety does not depend on the window' argument therefore fails once MVP instruments are authored. AC-IA-59 and AC-IA-144 would pass on the 70/102/113/113/145 figures while the real lint fails. The window radius is spike-gated, so this is not blocking, but the safety claim is stated as a guarantee.
findings.fix: State in IA-37, D.10 and AC-IA-59 that the 175/145 figures exclude INSTRUMENT (home 9, A 4-5, B 5) and CONSOLE (4) subjects. Add instruments and consoles to `F` (or to a named term) in D.10. Rewrite the runtime-safety sentence so it rests on the window lint at `SUBJECT_WINDOW_HOPS` (derive at spike) and not on 'window <= loaded sum <= 192'. Record that the D.17 cumulative case (S_total 196-198 > 192; {home+B} 130 > 120) is the spike's pass line, and route it to Derelict Authoring and Emitter State.

findings.section: IA-41 / UI Requirements / Cross-References row 1260 / AC-IA-64 / OQ 45 / registry input_view
findings.finding: G1 and R2 are not applied to the HUD read list. (a) Interaction still defines and names `input_view(seat) {hold_pm, armed, device_class, pressed_action}` (L313, L336, L1147, L1174, L1416, L1554). The Controller publishes `confirm_view = {b, mode, armed, pressed, released, give_up_live}` (player-controller L593, L881, AC-PCI-145). The HUD consumes `confirm_view` (hud L183). The registry keeps `input_view` only 'as the registered alias ... until Interaction and HUD conform', with source: still interaction-system.md although the owner is the Controller. (b) The result-event record is `{seat, command_id, queued_tick, kind}` (L313, L1152, L1157, L1416, AC-IA-139). `command_id` is not a kernel term. Kernel R2 stamps seq internally, keeps submit() void and echoes a caller-attached opaque `correlation` (kernel L87, L108, KRN-SEQ-05; player-controller L124 keys pre-play by it). AC-IA-64's allow-list lint (`hud_read_allowlist.json`) would reject a HUD built to the Controller and HUD GDDs.
findings.fix: Rename `input_view` to `confirm_view` in IA-41, UI Requirements, the Cross-References rows, AC-IA-64, OQ 45 and the Dependencies HUD row, and list the Controller's fields (b = hold_pm / 1000, mode, armed, pressed, released, give_up_live). Replace `command_id` with `correlation` in the result-event record and AC-IA-139. Ask the registrar to move the `input_view`/`confirm_view` source: to player-controller-input.md.

findings.section: IA-41 / Cross-References section 3 / OQ 49 vs HUD & Suit Layer; owed-refresh rows

findings.section: IA-1 / IA-3 / IA-10 / Dependencies engine note vs kernel R3 (CR-19 callable contract)
findings.finding: The kernel's R3 contract (kernel L152-153): every kernel-invoked owner callable (validate, apply, step hooks, snapshot, restore, post_restore, read_view) takes `ctx` and its only return is `return ctx.complete()`, with results through ctx.ok()/ctx.reject(). Interaction never mentions it (grep for `ctx` and `complete()` returns nothing). IA-10 says `validate` 'returns the first of' the reasons, and engine item (1) (L918) speaks of 'typed validate()/apply()' handler bases. A story author following Interaction builds returning validates that the kernel treats as faulted. The prior pass listed this and it did not land.
findings.fix: Add one conformance sentence to IA-1/Conventions: all Interaction validate, apply, hook, read_view and restore callables follow kernel CR-19 (ctx, `return ctx.complete()`), and 'returns a reason' means ctx.reject(reason). Reword engine item (1) to the CompletionToken form. Add a lint row (L-CODE) that no Interaction callable returns anything but ctx.complete().

findings.section: AC-IA-110 vs IA-36 post_restore / States 8 / Save/Load REBASE_BLOCKS
findings.finding: AC-IA-110 (L1401) requires 'snapshot-restore-snapshot with every table populated is byte-identical'. IA-36 post_restore drops every in-progress channel (the persisted seat `channel{...}` record) and clears `last_result`/`prev_result` (L303, States 8 L439). A snapshot taken with a channel and a last_result populated cannot equal the post-restore snapshot. Save/Load puts interaction.state in REBASE_BLOCKS ('a restore normalisation, OQ-39', save-load L300). Interaction never mentions REBASE_BLOCKS, and its OQ 39 is an unrelated row, so the reference dangles. The row is untestable as written.
findings.fix: Rewrite AC-IA-110: 'byte-identical for ledger, full_jobs, throws, loose, stubs, last_salvage_T and counters; the seat channel record and last_result/prev_result are normalised by post_restore and compared under REBASED rules'. findings.section: IA-41 press_blocked_moving / IA-10 BUSY / States 2 / AC-IA-142
findings.finding: `press_blocked_moving` is true on 'CHANNEL and HOLD_CONFIRM plates' (L324), with the stated meaning 'a `begin_*` press would be answered BUSY'. The BUSY-while-moving rule is on `begin_*` only (IA-10 L181; States 2 L371). V6 is a HOLD_CONFIRM `set_opening` and is not a `begin_*`. Nothing makes a V6 hold BUSY while moving, so the hollow-keycap tell on a V6 plate predicts a reject that does not occur. The tell must not lie. `field_check` is a CHANNEL verb with no `begin_` prefix, so the rule's wording leaves it unclassified (the hook abort at e = 0 covers the outcome). AC-IA-142 fixtures cover only CHANNEL and TAP.
findings.fix: Define the field by the declaration: true iff the row's mode is CHANNEL (every channel verb, `field_check` included, requires `intent_octant == NONE` at validate). Remove HOLD_CONFIRM from L324 and the HUD row, or state explicitly that a V6 hold is rejected BUSY while moving and add that to IA-10. Replace 'at a `begin_*`' with 'at a CHANNEL-mode verb' in IA-10 and AC-IA-18b. Add a V6 fixture to AC-IA-142.

findings.section: D.1b bead_segments / AC-IA-143 (auto half) / registry bead_segments
findings.finding: The re-leak times 'about 250 s, 340 s and 440 s' mix the upper bound of the first discrete window with the lower bounds of the others. Graph LS-23 and D.9: wear 100 bp lands only on `step_no mod WEAR_PERIOD_STEPS (100) = 0`, after a 2400-step hold, and LEAK returns when hp < 4000. From a banked h the number of wear ticks needed is floor((h - 4000)/100) + 1 = 1, 11, 21. The first tick falls 0.1-10 s after the hold, depending on phase. Windows: 4000 -> 240.1-250 s, 5000 -> 340.1-350 s, 6000 -> 440.1-450 s after the last PATCH step. 'About' cannot be asserted in an (auto) step. The variable table also says h is 4000..6000 for a patched subject. A patch cancelled before step 10 (hp 3001..3999, hp_cap already 6000) leaves h under LEAK_HP. The formula's clamp still returns 1, but the stated range is wrong and the D.1b header promises a non-negative operand clamp it does not show.
findings.fix: Rewrite the AC-IA-143 auto half: 'THEN the re-leak tick is the first wear tick (step_no multiple of 100) after patched_at_step + 2400 at which hp < LEAK_HP: within [240.1, 250] s, [340.1, 350] s and [440.1, 450] s of the last step'. Use the same windows in D.1b, Player Fantasy, OQ 41 and the registry output text. Write the formula as clamp(1 + floori(2 * max(0, h - LEAK_HP) / (PATCH_CAP_BP - LEAK_HP)), 1, 3) and widen the h range to 0..6000 with a note that h under 4000 gives one segment.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: untestable rows (quoted) with rewrites
findings.finding: Rows that a QA tester cannot execute as written. (a) AC-IA-143 auto: 'the Graph's re-leak times after completion are about 250 s, 340 s and 440 s'. (b) AC-IA-93: 'a grep of this GDD for PATCH_CAP_BP and PATCH_DECAY_S finds only the values 6000 and 240 (and the re-leak figures derived from them ...)'. data.summary: Fourth pass, read-only, no BLOCKING findings. The verdict is APPROVED with RECOMMENDED fixes (the previous log verdict was NEEDS REVISION). Script results: gdd-structure-check shows all 8 sections PRESENT. review-receipts reports CHANGED for the GDD and the registry, as expected after the R12-R21 pass. Dependencies check: 25 of 26 systems have a GDD on disk and only Onboarding is undesigned (R9, not a blocker). All three prior blockers are RESOLVED, in this file and in the siblings they named. They are the D39 bead vs FT-32 (the bead is now drawn on the IW-18 patch plate; PATCH_WEEP is a separate static mark), `body.state` in `restore_after` (acyclic), and the door `set_opening` carry-admitted sweep (AC-IA-78 now agrees with AC-IA-99b, and Controller PC-8 carries the door).
